query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small Sn alloying addition (~2–5 at.%) to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance by promoting the in-situ formation of a protective, Sn-rich oxide scale during high-temperature exposure.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr with its known microstructure and mechanical properties (8–16% room-temperature ductility; yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C).
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled Sn addition (approximately 2–5 atomic percent) into the equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy during casting.
generation.conditions: Exposure to air at around 800 °C for 5 hours, under loading conditions similar to those in previous high-temperature mechanical tests (strain rates of 10^(-4)–10^(-2) s^(-1)).
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a continuous, adherent Sn-rich oxide (likely SnO2) layer on the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: During high-temperature exposure, Sn segregates to the surface and oxidizes preferentially, forming a stable and protective SnO2 scale that acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion. This protective oxide layer reduces the inward diffusion of oxygen, thereby mitigating the oxidation (or pesting) that limits high-temperature performance.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Sn-doped HfNbTaTiZr alloy will exhibit a markedly lower oxidation rate and improved resistance to pesting during 5-hour exposure at 800 °C compared to the undoped alloy, while preserving its useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
generation.baseline: Undoped, equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr, which shows inadequate oxygen resistance (prone to pesting) at high temperatures despite acceptable room- and high-temperature mechanical properties.
generation.boundary: The protective effect is expected in an air atmosphere at approximately 800 °C for exposures around 5 hours, under similar strain rate conditions used in previous studies (10^(-4)–10^(-2) s^(-1)). Effects outside this temperature, time, or mechanical loading regime require further investigation.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the optimal Sn concentration and the potential for any adverse effects on mechanical properties. Additionally, while Sn is a promising candidate based on related studies, similar benefits from other alloying additions such as Ge or B were reported and might require comparative evaluation.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr specimens: one set doped with ~3 at.% Sn and one set as the control with no Sn addition. Subject both sets to a 5-hour exposure in air at 800 °C under comparable mechanical loading conditions (strain rates of 10^(-4)–10^(-2) s^(-1)).
measurements: Surface and cross-sectional oxide scale characterization using SEM/EDX and XRD to verify the formation, composition, and continuity of the Sn-rich oxide layer.
Weight gain measurements to quantify oxidation rates.
Room-temperature and high-temperature tensile tests to assess retention of ductility and yield strength.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Sn-doped specimens do not show a statistically significant reduction in oxidation rate (by weight gain and oxide scale characterization) or if their mechanical properties degrade relative to the undoped control, then the hypothesis that Sn addition improves oxygen resistance is falsified.

chosen.approach: Alloying additions (Sn, Ge, or B) to form protective oxide scale
